svg.title: sky jobs launch workflow on ej-prj-i3-2
svg.text: sky jobs launch: workflow, functions, line numbers and measured times
Code: ej-prj-i3-2 d771518f1 (on master 796c5bcc8). Consolidation mode (sky api start --deploy). Task: ej/task_bytecode.yaml, 6 nodes on k8s/kind-skypilot, one echo.
Times are medians in seconds. The letter beside a time says where it comes from. O1–O15 mark the rows each optimization changed; the list is at the bottom.

Largest stage left in D, down from 16.28 s on the base
before all changes. Skylet finishes first, so the wait for
workers to join sets the time.
Without gRPC, each starts Python on the head over kubectl
exec. gRPC is off by default. _add_job runs on into E.
From queue → last rank. Not visible from the server. T
rows are an older trace on the published image, 8.32 s in
all, so bytecode has likely cut the import rows.
Overlaps E, so it does not set E's length. It does decide
when the status check runs, and so sets F. Caller of the
Check status, mark the job RUNNING
Both are head commands. The first began before the job
ended; 0.97 s of it falls in F.
No recorded wait: no head command when the launch already
saw SUCCEEDED. Otherwise: wait up to 15 s, then one
command for status and end time.
Follower waits for saved logs, then exits
SUCCEEDED usually arrives before the follower tails the
cluster (10 of 11 runs), so a short job's logs appear in
one burst at the end. The rest of H is the client's own
Save logs and tear down the cluster
Starts after SUCCEEDED. The client waits for the log copy
but not for the probe or teardown, which runs on after it

Phase numbers beside each band: ej-prj-i2-6 → ej-prj-i3-2, same session, 8 runs per arm, launches about 40 s apart, with the permutation p. Client total 41.31 → 37.06 s (p = 0.013). Only phase A changes
significantly. Two of the 8 patched runs hit an expired record, with A about 7 s; the other 6 were 1.6–2.6 s. Launches more than 10 minutes apart get no saving.

Breakdown: this branch adds only the storage check reuse to ej-prj-i2-6, so B–H rows and phase A's client rows come from the i2-6 traced session and were not rerun here. Its phase medians are in the table
above, so they can differ from the band numbers. Time to read the record was not timed; phase A's rows already add up to its A/B median. 1 of 15 traced launches failed at submission.

Phase C keeps its aws configure list: get_cloud_credential_file_mounts is a separate path from the storage check. C was 0.98 vs 3.42 s without and with aws on the API server's PATH (20261102-aws-path-test), and
aws.remote_identity: NO_UPLOAD removes the call. Without aws on the PATH, the storage check also costs less, so the reuse saves less.

Against master, no allowed_clouds or NO_UPLOAD on either side: 796c5bcc8 + published image → ej-prj-i3-2 + bytecode image, 74.3 → 34.2 s for sky jobs launch and 46.70 → 27.57 s for sky launch, both p = 0.0002
(20261103-i3-2-vs-master-no-tips). This branch does not include the ej-prj-i3-1 rsync change.

Overlap: rows do not always add up to their box. Pods bootstrap while the provisioner runs, skylet starts during the Ray wait, and the controller's checks overlap E and H. T times predate later commits and show

Conditions: 6 nodes on kind, one machine, IfNotPresent with the local bytecode image, gRPC off, consolidation mode, aws on the server PATH. The first launch after a server restart is slower (warm-ups were
dropped). The bytecode image is not published.
Not shown: failure and recovery paths, and _submit_remotely() without consolidation mode.
